title: Norn Project Web 2.1.0
scope: A local EN/FR Web interface for project managers, distributed with arka-norn and backed exclusively by existing Project, Feature, Pipeline, document, audit, Agent and orchestration contracts.
objective: Make every managed Project understandable and actionable without requiring terminal fluency, while preserving signed documents, traceability, local security and native-agent boundaries.

assumptions.subject: Distribution
assumptions.selected_position: Ship a complete loopback Web application in 2.1.0; keep Tauri as a separate phase 2 Feature behind the same typed bridge.

assumptions.subject: Agent boundary
assumptions.selected_position: Display registered Agents and observe Norn orchestrations, but never start, stop, retry, configure or grant permissions to Agents from the Web interface.

assumptions.subject: Governance
assumptions.selected_position: Keep framework documents immutable and record human decisions as append-only, portable Project governance events signed by a stable local human profile.

executive_summary: Norn Project Web turns the existing local framework into a project-tracking workspace for non-developers. It presents Project health, Feature progress, workflow relationships, every signed document, audits, decisions, registered Agents and live orchestration state through human-readable projections. The filesystem contracts remain the source of truth and the browser receives only bounded, authenticated read models.
guiding_principle: The interface explains the Project; it never becomes a second source of truth or a remote control for Agents.

sections.title: Audience and experience
sections.content: The primary user is a project manager who needs to understand progress, evidence, risks, dependencies and decisions without reading JSON or operating coding-agent tools. The default view answers where the Project stands, what requires attention and which evidence supports that conclusion.

sections.title: Information architecture
sections.content: The product is organized around Projects, Features, workflow stages, documents, decisions, audits, Agents and activity. Stable resource routes support refresh and deep links. A deterministic relationship graph complements, rather than replaces, the ordered workflow view.

sections.title: Human documents and decisions
sections.content: All canonical v5 and supported legacy documents receive one schema-driven human rendering with provenance and dependency links. Raw JSON remains available as technical disclosure. Human decisions are append-only events linked to exact resources and never rewrite signed framework documents.

sections.title: Live observation
sections.content: executions.json remains the durable ledger. Filesystem changes emit lightweight authenticated invalidations and the client reloads complete projections. Heartbeats describe liveness only; the UI never invents cost, percentage or remaining time.

sections.title: Security and distribution
sections.content: The server binds only to loopback, uses an ephemeral session token, validates Origin and paths, applies a strict CSP and never exposes prompts, secrets, environment variables, stderr or raw terminal output. The same NornBridge boundary is reserved for a later Tauri shell.

recommendation: Implement as a Complete Feature and release only after Project tracking, document rendering, governance, audits, read-only live observation, EN/FR, accessibility and packaging gates pass together.
risks: A browser-facing filesystem bridge can widen the local attack surface unless every route is allowlisted and authenticated.
A generic document renderer can become unreadable unless semantic field presentations and relationship views are tested across every distributed schema.
Filesystem watchers can miss or duplicate notifications, so the durable ledger and full snapshot reload must remain authoritative.
The private mock can create false parity expectations unless unsupported agent-control and simulated metrics are removed explicitly.
